title: S224 capstone - one toggle, Number One did the rest
intro: Number One was switched on once against a fresh Mission parked at Verify on the S222 rewind build. Nobody prompted it again.

steps.caption: The captain's live LCARS board (his own viewscreen daemon, port 8790), cropped to the fresh capstone card in the Verify column just before Number One was switched on. The card reads "MBR View Builder (S224 capstone)", label lcars:verify, engine copilot, and the Number One row is EMPTY — no score, no headline, nothing. Estimate pills: $4.30-$28.39, reason HIGH, impl HIGH. Captured in headless Chrome at 430px wide, deviceScaleFactor 3; the PNG is 672 x 963 px.

The same card about 90 seconds after the single `lcars xo on --engine copilot` toggle. Number One has taken the conn by itself: an amber "NUMBER ONE · ENGAGED" pill, the line "Number One has the conn", a live "LAUNCHING…" state, and — the point — the captain's own VERIFY button is now struck out and disabled (dashed outline, ⊘) with a STAND DOWN offered in its place. Nobody typed anything after the toggle. 672 x 1091 px, headless Chrome, 430px viewport, deviceScaleFactor 3.

Thirty-one minutes after the toggle, with nobody prompting it: the capstone card now carries Number One's verdict — a red LOW pill reading "Couldn't check the point of the mission · 74 of 102 checked", a READ THE FULL REPORT button, an ACTUAL ~$9.76 pill beside the $4.30-$28.39 estimate, and the human VERIFY button replaced by "⊘ RESOLVING 4 LOGGED BUGS…" — it had already filed four bugs and started fixing them. 638 x 1389 px.

One of the four bugs Number One filed by itself, an hour after the toggle: GitHub Enterprise issue #220, "the Pull data & start button's oversized icon", now at lcars:plan, engine copilot, NUMBER ONE · ENGAGED, "Number One has the conn · Copilot", live progress "PLOTTING THE COURSE TO ENGINEERING… — WRITING OUTPUT". Nobody typed anything to make this happen; issues #220, #221, #222 and #223 were all filed and started in the same pass. 638 x 1154 px.

The left rail of Number One's report, cropped and enlarged 3x: "102 THINGS YOU ASKED FOR" with a three-colour bar — 70 worked, 4 didn't work, 28 I couldn't check — and the line "plus 5 I measured — never moves the grade". The S222 baseline's equivalent numbers on the same build were 101 things: 76 worked, 3 didn't work, 22 couldn't check. 645 x 684 px.

The verdict text and the two things Number One handed back to the captain rather than deciding itself. First "THIS ONE IS YOURS TO DECIDE": the planted automation trap — "The loaded snapshot (2026-07-27.0) has zero automatable/wired KPIs ... could not be observed on screen" — reported as unseeable, never as broken. Second: a finding nobody wrote a criterion for — the legend says "Moda" while three KPI rows label the same cohort "Mode" — ending "nobody asked about this; I saw it in shot-s0-part-01". Filters below: All 109, Didn't work 4, I measured 7, Couldn't check 28, Worked 70. 659 x 917 px.

blindTo: The four bugs it filed were still being fixed when these were taken - the single re-grade had not run yet.
Only the captain's own viewscreen board was photographed; Number One's own 27 walk shots live in the mission record, not here.
